name: Stratum MCP: Cloud Resource Control Plane
tag: See and control every cloud resource from one AI-ready control plane, with nothing changed until you approve.

scenarios.title: Explain a bill spike
scenarios.ask: Why did our cloud bill jump this month? We run {accounts} accounts.
steps: Inventory
Read {accounts} accounts: {=accounts * 42} resources across compute, storage and databases.
Cost agent
Bill up {=round(servers * size * 730 / (accounts * 2000) * 100)}%. Most of it is {servers} test servers left running since the 3rd.
Policy
Those servers have no owner tag, which breaks your tagging rule.
Action
Prepared a shutdown plan. Waiting for your approval before anything changes.
followups: What if someone still needs one of those servers?
The plan stops servers instead of deleting them, so any one can be restarted in minutes. Owners get a notice first and can reply to keep theirs.
How does it stop this from happening again?
Stratum can add a rule that pauses untagged test servers after 48 hours. You'd have saved about ${=round(servers * size * 24 * 25)} this month with that rule in place.
It works with the major public clouds through read-only access by default. Write access is added per action and only for what you approve.

scenarios.title: Tagging clean-up
scenarios.ask: Audit our {resources} resources for missing owner and cost-center tags. About {untagged}% look untagged.
steps: Inventory
Listed {resources} resources and their current tags.
Policy
Found {=round(resources * untagged / 100)} resources missing an owner or cost-center tag.
Owner finder
Matched {=round(resources * untagged / 100 * 0.7)} of them to an owner using creation logs and naming patterns.
Action
Drafted tag updates for the matched ones and a short list for a person to sort out.
followups: Why do tags matter so much?
Without an owner tag nobody gets the bill, so idle resources stay on. Tags also let finance split cloud cost by team.
Can it apply the tags in bulk?
Yes, once you approve the list. Each change is logged with who approved it, so it can be undone.

scenarios.title: Turn off dev at night
scenarios.ask: Our {devs} development servers only get used {usage} a day. Schedule them to sleep the rest of the time.
steps: Usage reader
Checked 30 days of activity on {devs} servers. Busy hours cluster in a {usage}-hour window on weekdays.
Scheduler
Proposed a wake/sleep schedule: on {usage} hours each weekday, off nights and weekends.
Safety check
Excluded servers running long jobs or tagged as always-on.
Action
Prepared the schedule. Anyone can wake a server early from chat.
followups: What if a developer works late?
They ask the control plane to wake their server and it's up in a few minutes. The schedule resumes the next night.
No, they're an estimate from the hourly rate and the schedule. Actual savings depend on your pricing and how often servers get woken early.
